title: Charlie, Clare and the Monkey

story: Charlie and Clare live in the **country**. Today they are in the **city**.
“**Come on!**” says Clare. “The **circus** is in the **city centre**.”
They leave the car in a **car park** and walk to the town **centre**.
It is **cold**, so Charlie puts on his **coat**.
First they stop at a **café** next to the **cinema**.
Mum has a **cup** of **coffee**. The children have bread and **cheese**.
The **cook** comes out of the kitchen. “I can **cook** eggs for you too,” he says.
“No, thank you,” says Clare. “We must **catch** the bus to the circus.”
Charlie brings his **comic book**. His favourite **comic** is about a **clown**.
The bus stops, and the children see a big red tent.
Outside the tent, a man draws a big **circle** in the sand.
A clown with **curly** hair jumps into the circle.
He is very **clever**. He can **climb** a rope with one hand.
His **CD** player plays music, and everyone laughs.
A little boy **cries** because he cannot see the clown.
The clown lifts the boy up, and now the boy laughs too.
Next to the tent, there is a big **cage**.
A small monkey lives in it. Her name is Nina.
“Be **careful**,” says the clown. “Nina can open doors.”
He opens the cage **carefully**, but Nina jumps out.
She takes Charlie’s comic book and runs away.
“**Come on**, Clare!” shouts Charlie.
There is one grey **cloud**. Then the sky is **cloudy**.
Nina runs past the café and out into the **countryside**.
Charlie runs too fast, and now he has a **cough**.
“We cannot catch her,” says Clare. “We must **change** our plan.”
She walks back to the café and asks the cook for some cheese.
Then she **calls** Nina and holds the cheese up high.
Nina **could** climb trees when she was small, and she climbs down one now.
She gives the comic book back and takes the cheese.
Charlie **carries** Nina to the clown.
“You are a clever boy,” laughs the clown, “but Nina is clever too.”
Then he draws a little monkey in Charlie’s comic book.

options: She could climb trees when she was small

retell: Charlie and Clare go to the circus in the city.
A monkey jumps out of her cage and takes the comic book.
Clare brings some cheese and calls the monkey.
Nina gives the book back and Charlie carries her home.

reading: Read 1 - You read the story out loud. The child only listens. No dictionary.
Read 2 - Stop at every dark word. Let the child guess it from the picture in the story.
Read 3 - Ask the five questions. Short answers are fine.
Read 4 - The child retells the story in four sentences.
teaching: careful is an adjective for a person: be careful. carefully says how you do it: open the cage carefully.
catch here means to be in time for a bus or a train, not to catch a ball with your hands.
could is can in the past, for something you were able to do: she could climb trees when she was small.
the country is the green place outside the city; a country is also a land like Japan. The countryside is the fields you can see there.
come on! is not come + on. It means hurry up, let us go.
